correctness.rationale: An order-preserving partial isometry on [n] is a partial translation. For fixed nonzero displacement d, domain masks split into d residue chains; ν(f)=one plus longest consecutive-one run, and every nonzero such shift is nilpotent. The finite-state no-k-run generating function is derived by terminal and nonterminal blocks, and product over the chains gives the stated complete rank/height polynomial including the one empty map. For fixed d, isolated starts of k-runs have factorial moments approaching (θ/2)^h; the geometric distribution of |d| permits truncation and mixing, giving e^{-θ/2}. Distinct endpoint and k=1 cases checked; independent mask/finite-automaton comparisons for 36 (n,k) pairs n≤8 agreed. Finite tests do not prove the lattice law.
